A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same retraining framework and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and theoretical and experimental appendices. Renumbered and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments and CIFAR, AG News, and CIFAR-100N training results, including additional comparisons in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds DomainNet experiments and further noise-robust training comparisons.

M1.justification: The full and consensus-based hard-label retraining rules and the analyzed linear classifiers are unchanged. Both experimental appendices specify restarting retraining from random initialization. Added backbones and base losses evaluate the retained retraining procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds the much larger, 345-class DomainNet image-classification dataset, substantially extending visual data coverage beyond CIFAR (Section 5, Tables 7–9). CIFAR-10/100, AG News, and the appendix's CIFAR-100N human-annotation setting are retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds reported retraining comparisons using Wang et al.'s symmetric cross-entropy on CIFAR-100 and Patrini et al.'s backward correction on DomainNet. v2 mentions these alternatives in a footnote but only tabulates forward-corrected initial training. The existing prior-based, randomized-response, and confidence-based comparisons remain.

E3.justification: DomainNet introduces linear probing on an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, a 90/10 training/validation split, and 15-epoch training stages. For retained CIFAR experiments, v2's 21k/28k gradient steps per stage become 30/40 epochs in v3. This revises the reported budgets; equivalence across differently sized retraining subsets, or rerunning the experiments, is not established.

E4.justification: The existing question of whether retraining remains useful after noise-robust training receives additional symmetric cross-entropy and backward-correction evidence, plus another forward-correction noise level. Capacity and no-validation analyses lose their epsilon = 3 ResNet-34 rows. Confidence filtering and human-annotation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three runs and mean ± standard deviation in experimental tables. The added results follow the same reporting practice; no new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure appears.

E6.justification: v3 adds DomainNet results, including 23.60/29.23/36.30% accuracy for baseline/full/consensus retraining at epsilon = 3 (Table 7), and additional noise-robust results in Tables 5, 6, 8, and 9. Most retained entries are numerically identical. The epsilon = 3 ResNet-34 rows from v2 Tables 4 and 10 disappear.

T1.justification: Remark 4.10 substantively revises the sufficient sample-size range and covariance assumptions; Remark 4.3 adds eigenvalue factors. Theorem 4.8 gains d ≥ 7, and v2 Lemma E.2's condition changes from less than 1 to greater than 1 in v3 Lemma F.2. v3 also supplies a proof of Lemma F.3. The accuracy-to-error reformulation is otherwise mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claimed improvement regime: its sample-size lower threshold changes from d log n/(1−2p) to [d/(1−2p)^2] log[d/(1−2p)^2]. This materially changes the guarantee near maximal label noise. The central novelty claim and the claim that consensus retraining improves label-DP training without additional privacy cost remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion suggesting the sample-size lower threshold is tight up to logarithms while the upper threshold may be a proof artifact. It also removes v2's blanket interpretation that ResNet-34 produces smaller retraining gains than ResNet-18. The main limitations concerning consensus theory and non-uniform noise remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds DomainNet's training schedule and baseline-specific learning rates, and specifies symmetric cross-entropy coefficients alpha = 0.8 and beta = 0.2. It revises CIFAR budget descriptions and removes v2's disclosure of one 40 GB A100 GPU per run. Frameworks, restart instructions, and BERT access links remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix E compares the lower bound with Cai and Wei (2021), Im and Grigas (2023), and Zhu et al. (2024). v3 also adds the DomainNet citation, removes Zhang and Sabuncu (2018), and drops the regularization contrast with Das and Sanghavi. The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The six main sections retain their order. Editing replaces 'vanilla training' with 'initial training', rewrites theoretical explanations around error, and updates affiliation and venue text. The AG News diagnostic discussion moves into an appendix, while impact and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: v3 extensively reformats the main text and references into an ICML two-column layout, resizing and redistributing displays. It adds four result tables, moves the AG News diagnostic table to Appendix I, and combines existing with/without-validation results in Table 14. Figure 1 retains its underlying scatter plots.

improvement.justification: DomainNet and explicit noise-robust comparisons broaden empirical support, while corrected lemma conditions and clearer discussion improve the theoretical presentation. These benefits are tempered by the unexplained CIFAR step-to-epoch budget revision, removed hardware disclosure, and loss of some high-noise ResNet-34 results. The evidence supports a limited overall quality improvement.
